# Ocean subscription security review

Review date: 2026-11-12. Donor: WSL043/dsh-codex-subscription 3.2.13, commit fb37c50a128aed84b230c520bf934cded97d851b. Locations below refer to that unmodified donor unless marked Ocean. The review inspected the main host entrypoints, credential storage, OAuth coordination, RPC routing, network transport, native runtime and remote-control surfaces. No personal credential files, OAuth login, provider requests or paid operations were used. This is a scoped source review, not a formal certification of all 27,698 lines of JS/JSX or all transitive dependencies.

## Delivered restrictions

Ocean exposes subscription sign-in, account management, model selection and quota. `src/ocean-policy.js` constrains loaded settings and rejects enabling writes before persistence. Advanced remote control, voice, predictions, connectors, images, subscription search/fetch and native Codex execution remain unavailable, not merely hidden in UI. Automatic quota retries, cloud compaction, reasoning-cache modification and WebSocket connection mode are locked off. Ocean web registries and configured providers are left untouched: donor registry mutation, registration and selection paths were removed from application startup. Diagnostics remain in memory without automatic disk attachment. Plugin state paths use ocean-codex-subscription rather than donor cache directories.

An RPC allowlist rejects advanced and unknown endpoints before calling their implementation. A network-area allowlist additionally blocks advanced provider calls outside the RPC bridge. Only login, OAuth, model, quota and catalog network operations are permitted. This is capability containment, not a general URL firewall. Native Codex subagent registration was removed. The remote relay environment override was removed. OAuth credentials use `OCEAN_CODEX_SUBSCRIPTION_OAUTH` and `ocean-codex-subscription/accounts`, without importing prior OPENAI/WSL043 references. The vault retains its own Ocean string reference for its existing compatibility implementation, not as a route to donor credentials.

## Findings and mitigation rationale

1. Upstream images are enabled by default (`src/image-features.js:3–7`), search defaults to auto (`src/settings-contract.js:17`) and other-model access defaults on (`src/preference-fields.js`). Registration in `src/index.js:422` can expose image tools. These defaults were inappropriate for an authentication-only first release; constrained settings and network policy prevent activation.
2. Off settings alone do not gate all RPCs: `src/subscription-rpc.js:123–153` allows voice catalog/preview and remote enable/pair calls directly; `:163–173` exposes runtime changes; `:338–374` exposes quota-reset consumption. Ocean denies these whole endpoint families, including crafted requests.
3. Native subagent registration occurs independently of the backend selector (`src/index.js:385`). Its thread policy uses approvalPolicy never and inherited sandbox mode (`src/subagent-backend.js:24,76`). Ocean does not register this provider. Upstream disables apps/plugins/browser features; that is not a substitute for reviewing execution authority.
4. Existing credential references and legacy migration (`src/index.js:81–83,165–173`, `src/account-vault.js:173–195,334,361–362`) could reuse unrelated authorizations. Ocean names are isolated and donor legacy refs removed. The host credential service owns at-rest protection; its actual platform encryption was not verified here.
5. Catalog refresh starts during plugin application (`src/index.js:510`); an already authorized Ocean account can refresh OAuth and contact the provider on future launches. Signed-out operation must remain inert. Credentials are not supplied by this review.
6. The transport's CODEX_HOSTS set is not a deny-by-default firewall: other hosts pass to original fetch (`src/oauth-network.js:210–213`). Global fetch/WebSocket wrappers use AsyncLocalStorage and cleanup (`:247–295`); concurrent lifecycle behavior requires regression coverage. OAuth is delegated to pi-ai, so behavior depends on the pinned dependency version.
7. Remote relay URLs accept HTTPS chatgpt.com subdomains and HTTP loopback (`src/remote-control-relay.js:51–60`). Remote methods can change session permission presets (`src/remote-control-dsh.js:905–913`) and expose session/history/device functions. Remote remains server-blocked; an environment variable cannot reactivate it.
8. Connector write mode bypasses per-call approval; ask mode demands allowed-once and read mode trusts tool metadata (`src/connectors.js:222–233`). All connector modes remain locked off.
9. Optional Codex CLI installation is pinned to 0.167.0 with --ignore-scripts and profile ownership checks (`src/subagent-cli.js:7–8,48–52`). Tokens are passed over private JSON-RPC rather than argv/env/auth.json (`src/subagent-auth.js:75–79`). Neither install/remove nor native execution is enabled in Ocean.
10. Upstream diagnostic logging uses regex redaction but appendFileSync has no explicit private file mode (`src/diagnostic-log.js:35`, `src/diagnostic-log-format.js`). Redaction is not a guarantee against every secret pattern. Failure captures mask text but retain selected identifiers (`src/failure-capture.js`). Ocean disables automatic disk log attachment; in-memory diagnostics still require user review before sharing. Do not automatically upload support diagnostics. Private log permissions and stricter field allowlists remain recommended hardening work.

## Data destinations and licensing

The retained donor OAuth/model implementation uses auth.openai.com and chatgpt.com/backend-api subscription endpoints, including codex responses/models and wham usage/profile/history. This is not a completed migration to the new official Sign in with ChatGPT dynamic-client integration. MIT licensing of source does not establish provider authorization, policy compliance or availability of these endpoints. User sign-in and any real subscription operation require a separate explicit handoff and validation.

Preserve LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. They contain WSL043 and other MIT notices plus references to Apache-2.0 Codex. The donor notices list Codex 0.153.4 while its optional installer pins 0.167.0; the latter is not installed by this integration. Transitive license coverage and any third-party image/brush asset rights need separate packaging review before distribution.

## Verification and limits

Ran offline: `node --test tests/ocean-policy.test.mjs tests/settings-adapter.test.mjs`: 8 tests passed. These cover loaded-settings constraints, rejected writes without side effects, all advanced RPC names plus unknown routes, network-area denial, permitted core routing, credential-isolation source checks and settings-adapter compatibility. No real tokens were used.

These focused tests do not prove the complete desktop build, live OAuth success, all upstream tests, cross-platform behavior or service-policy compatibility. Desktop bundle validation, UI verification, no-network signed-out startup, login interruption/account-switch/refresh-race testing and a real authorized model response remain separate completion criteria. This report records the restricted initial integration, not approval to re-enable excluded integrations.
